prompts.remote_wrapper:
You are working on the project {project} with Metaform. Metaform holds the project's functional map: what each part of the project is for, and how the parts serve one another.
The file uploaded with this message, {wheel}, is Metaform carrying the project. It is a Python wheel that runs directly with Python 3.11 or newer, with no install and no network.
1. Run it first, from an empty folder of its own, which becomes the project's folder: `python {wheel}`, with the path to where the file was uploaded. The first run registers the project, unpacks its files into that folder when the wheel carries them, opens your working layer, and prints Metaform's instructions, the map's entry and how to return your work. Read all of it. 2. Run each Metaform command the same way, from that folder: `python {wheel} <command>`. `python {wheel} help` lists the commands, and `python {wheel} help <command>` explains one. 3. Record on the map what you learn and decide as you work. A write that names no layer goes to your working layer, and your working layer is what travels back to the person. 4. Return your work with `python {wheel} return note="<what you did, and what is left>"`. It writes one archive holding your working layer, your file changes and your note, and prints where the archive is. Offer that archive to the person as a download. Each return writes a new archive with all of your work so far.
Your task:
{task}
prompts.remote_onboarding:
Get to know this project, then follow the person's instructions.
1. Run the wheel and read everything it prints. 2. Take in the map from its entry: the elements and joins it shows are where the project starts. Read further around any address with `python {wheel} map where <address>`. 3. Tell the person what the project is and what it is for, as the map shows it, in a few short paragraphs. 4. Tell the person which Metaform commands you have, and that your work comes back to them through `python {wheel} return` as an archive they download. 5. Then follow the person's instructions in chat.

choose_agent.title: Agent, model and thinking level for ticket
choose_agent.why: Agents and models differ in what they do well and what they cost, so the choice is made once per ticket and kept where the person can see it.
choose_agent.ask:
Which agent in `agents` should work the ticket `
`, judged by what each agent's description says it does well?
choose_agent.model:
If the agent works the ticket `
`, which of its models in `options..model` should it run? Prefer the lighter model when the ticket is small and well defined, and the stronger one when it needs design, wide reading or care with risk.
choose_agent.thought_level:
If the agent works the ticket `
`, which thinking level in `options..thought_level` should it use? Prefer the lower level when the ticket is small and well defined, and the higher one when it needs design, wide reading or care with risk.

start_order.title: Tickets ordered for starting
start_order.why: Agents start the tickets the person has not placed on the board in this order; the ones the person placed keep their place.
start_order.ask:
Should the ticket `
` be started before the other tickets in `tickets`?
start_order.true: It unblocks other tickets in `tickets`, fixes a fault other work waits on, or is small, clear and ready to start.
start_order.false: It builds on other tickets in `tickets`, waits on an answer from the person, or can wait without holding other work up.

rank_items.title: Items ranked for the brief of
rank_items.why: A node's brief holds about 2 KB, so the items an agent at the node needs most are named first.
rank_items.ask:
Will an agent about to work at the node in `node` need the item `
` to do that work well?
rank_items.true: The item records a decision, a constraint, a fault, open work or a finding that bears on the node's operative purpose or on how the node is realized now.
rank_items.false: The item is about another node, has been superseded by a later item, or is background the agent can do without.

triage.title: Messages sorted for the person or an agent
triage.why: Every message stays on the person's list; those that need the person come first, and the rest are marked as ones an agent may answer.
triage.ask:
Does the message `
` need the person, rather than an agent, to act on it or answer it?
triage.true: It needs a decision only the person can make: a choice between options they care about, a permission, spending, a credential, a change of scope or of the CQU's goals, or knowledge only the person holds.
triage.false: An agent with the project's map, tools and source can act on it or answer it, however large the work.

intake_coverage.title: Top-level parts of the AUE checked against the map
intake_coverage.why: Every top-level part of the AUE is represented in the map, so no part is worked on without its purpose known.
intake_coverage.ask:
Is the top-level part `
` of the AUE represented in the map in `map`?
intake_coverage.true: An element in `map` stands for this part, for what it does, or for a collection that holds it.
intake_coverage.false: Nothing in `map` stands for this part or for what it does.

session_drift.title: Session checked for conclusion-reading, drift and repeats
session_drift.why: An agent that acts on earlier conclusions in place of the AUE inherits their errors, one that strays spends the person's budget on work nobody asked for, and one that repeats itself spends it on nothing.

conclusions.ask:
Do later calls in `calls` open the source that the document read in `
` describes?
conclusions.true: A later call opens, runs or changes the files, nodes or data the document describes.
conclusions.false: No later call opens what the document describes; the agent goes on from the document alone.

off_task.ask:
Does the call `
` read or change what the work in `task` needs?
off_task.true: It opens, runs or changes something the work in `task` needs, including reading to understand it.
off_task.false: It touches files, nodes or questions the work in `task` does not need.

repeating.ask:
Do the steps in `
` repeat work or checks already reported earlier in `steps`?
repeating.true: The steps re-read, re-verify or re-state the same things without new results.
repeating.false: Each step adds something new toward the work in `task`.
